title: CueFX cue file v2.6
description: Shape and types only. Value rules (8k+1 windows, frames inside the clip, enums such as hand or easing_in, ranges such as opacity 0..1) are checked by `validate`, which returns them with their own codes. All ranges are [start, end): start included, end excluded. Coordinates are plate pixels, origin top-left, y down; values outside the frame are allowed. Top-level fields not listed here are kept but reported (unknown_field).

version.description: "2.3" (written by new cues); "2.4" (a cue that sets body_point); "2.5" (a cue that sets shape or spin_deg_per_s); "2.6" (a cue that sets a non-fade ending or behaviour charge_up or orbit, or an orbit block); "2.2" files are read as they are, "2.1" files are read and upgraded to 2.2. Anything else: version_unsupported.

behaviour.description: v2.3. hold_throw | hold | charge_up (v2.6) | orbit (v2.6); missing means hold_throw. hold: the effect stays on the hand for the whole window; release_frame is null and route is []. charge_up (v2.6): as hold_throw (needs release_frame and route), and from appear_frame to release_frame the effect grows from 0.6x to 1.0x its size (smoothstep) and pulses at 3.5 Hz by +-8 % of size and brightness. orbit (v2.6): no release and no route (as hold; release_frame null, route []): the effect circles the body point on the `orbit` circle, bigger and brighter at the front, smaller and dimmer at the back. Any other value: behaviour_invalid.

orbit.description: v2.6. The circle of behaviour orbit; each missing field takes its default (GET /api/defaults -> orbit: radius 1.5 sizes, 180 deg/s, tilt 60; the tilt of a head is 80). Values outside the limits: orbit_invalid.

radius_sizes.description: radius in size measures of the body point, above 0, up to 10

speed_deg_per_s.description: degrees per second, the sign is the direction, within 3600

tilt_deg.description: tilt of the circle's plane: 0 = a full circle seen from the front, 90 = edge on; 0 to 90

shape.description: v2.5. sphere | ring | crystal | cube; missing means sphere. What the layout and the stand-in draw (ring: tilted torus; crystal: elongated octahedron; cube). `diameter_px` is the shape's outer size on screen. Any other value: shape_invalid.

spin_deg_per_s.description: v2.5. Spin of the shape in degrees per second (sign = direction, 0 = no spin). Missing means the shape's default: sphere 288 (as before), ring 90, crystal 60, cube 60.

ending.description: v2.6. fade | burst | shatter; missing means fade. How the effect ends at vanish.start. fade: Merge fades it out linearly over vanish (as before). burst: it grows fast to 1.8x and flashes bright, then fades (at least 0.3 s). shatter: 12-20 grey shards (count and directions from `seed`) fly outward, spin, fall a little and fade (at least 0.5 s). For burst and shatter Merge applies no fade-out of its own; if the vanish is shorter than the ending needs, `cue/normalize` lengthens vanish.end (warning vanish_extended). Any other value: ending_invalid.

canvas_rect.description: [x, y, w, h] in plate pixels

body_point.description: v2.4. What the effect follows. Missing means {part: palm, side: <hand>}. part: palm | fist | foot | knee | shoulder | head; side: the person's left | right, null only for head. The palm's side must equal `hand`. Any other value: body_point_invalid. hand_seed is the artist's click, or for a seedless non-palm cue/new request, the real tracked sample returned as analyze_result.body_point_seed.

part.description: palm | fist | foot | knee | shoulder | head

side.description: left | right (the person's); null for head

track.description: cue-file form of the track; the API's track (track.schema.json) maps to it

anchor_offset.description: orb centre minus palm centre, plate px

x.description: null only on route[0]: derived from the track

easing_in.description: linear | ease_in | ease_out | ease_in_out: shapes the time of the segment that ends at this point

reference_image.description: UI field: file name of the uploaded still (accepted for generate)

spill.description: UI field 'spill on occluders' (accepted, not used yet)

interaction.description: parked (interaction pass, tasks 14-16); kept as is

advanced.description: UI fields. Corrections are NOT here: they are the top-level `corrections`.
